Danny Jones hosts a CIA spy and an FBI agent who claim to bare the truth about UFOs and China. The episode title promises a double insider account. The guests are not named in the title, which puts the weight on their past posts.

The two men give their read on what the state knows about craft it cannot name. They link that secret to the race with China for the tech in those craft. Jones asks where their proof runs out. Listeners get spy talk on the two hottest files in the field. The library files the talk as an archive record.
podcast-joerogan-2TPyx-H1MVc:
Episode 517 of the Joe Rogan Experience features Crash, the founder of Float Lab, a maker of sensory deprivation tanks. Rogan is a longtime user of float tanks, and this early episode helped bring the practice to his huge audience. The guest speaks from years of building and testing the tanks.

Crash explains how floating in dark, salt-heavy water quiets the body and mind. He and Rogan trade stories about long floats, strange thoughts, and the calm that follows. Their talk covers pain, stress, and creative thinking, and it shows why floating moved from a fringe habit to a common wellness practice.
podcast-joerogan-ZIWnAR156Vc:
Russian soldiers turned to stone after shooting down a UFO is the legend Rogan tells in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience. The story, drawn from a reported declassified file, claims troops fired on a craft and were petrified by a flash from the beings who emerged. It is kept here as an archive tale, not as fact.

Rogan walks through the story's beats and its paper trail, such as it is. He asks why such tales attach to secret files and Cold War fears. The segment preserves a piece of UFO folklore in full, for listeners who study how these legends form and spread.
podcast-joerogan-efJ1-q3XxVc:
Comedian David Cross joins Joe Rogan for episode 2484. Cross co-created the cult sketch show Mr. Show. His stand-up has skewered power for three decades.

Rogan and Cross come from different wings of comedy and politics. That gap gives the talk its spark and care. They trade views on fame, faith, and the state of jokes. Cross stays witty and sharp throughout. The episode suits fans of alt comedy who want a veteran's take, and a rare meeting across a real divide. Respect survives their gaps in taste and tribe.
